answer: Found the Cambridge Dictionary Grammar guidelines on indirect speech at https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/reported-speech-indirect-speech (article 'Reported speech: indirect speech'). Guidelines: indirect speech focuses more on the content of what someone said rather than their exact words; the structure of the reported clause depends on whether the speaker is reporting a statement, a question or a command. Examples of changing direct speech to indirect speech: statement: '‘I’m tired,’ I said.' → 'I told them (that) I was tired.' (that-clause); question: '‘Are you ready?’ the nurse asked Joel.' → 'The nurse asked Joel if/whether he was ready.' (if/whether-clause), '‘Who are you?’ she asked.' → 'She asked me who I was.' (wh-clause); command: '‘Leave at once!’ they ordered.' → 'They ordered us to leave at once.' (to-infinitive clause). 'That' is often omitted in informal situations.
